scope: Independent readonly source review of fixed normal prefix evidence reader; no actual reader/device execution
checks: Source plan is read from the fixed root-private source directory and must match the external plan SHA, exact nonce/mode/scope and null predecessor before target evidence is accepted.

Held root-private directories and root-owned single-link mode0600 regular files with O_NOFOLLOW bound access. Every opened member descriptor closes in finally; registered directory descriptors close in reverse order.

Each member is limited to65536 bytes and checked across device/inode/mode/uid/gid/nlink/size/mtime/ctime before/after read. The eight evidence members have a262144-byte aggregate cap; the final text envelope is limited to524288 bytes. The plan has its own65536-byte member cap.

Expected-result mode requires exactly the externally supplied terminal-result SHA. Missing mode rejects a terminal result that was read. Nonempty evidence requires the matching original coordinator claim; every observed record requires the exact nonce, and any plan field must match.

All output has qualification_performed_by_reader=false; partial/missing evidence is explicitly listed. Reader success establishes bounded collection, not runtime success, process cleanup or namespace retirement.
The only file observation paths are the fixed plan and eight fixed owned evidence members. There is no unit, namespace, process-control, Android or Main mutation path.
scope_limitations: Expected-result mode can collect a failed runtime result or an incomplete evidence set. Consumers must qualify the producer result and required set separately; exit0 alone is not runtime PASS.

Missing-result mode observes absence at the initial member open (or directory lookup); it does not claim the result cannot be published later or that the multi-file read is an atomic terminal snapshot.
No real root-private device paths, actual directory metadata or producer outcome were read by this review. No synthetic I/O substitution test or repeated producer test was run.
